data.name: LibrarySubtitle
data.value: Automatic HDR for your selected games

data.name: EmptyBody
data.value: Add a game's EXE. The manager enables HDR before launch and restores the original state when you exit.

data.name: EnableDelayHelp
data.value: Launching through the manager enables HDR immediately, then waits 1 second before starting the game.

data.name: CoversInfo
data.value: Choose a portrait PNG, JPG or WEBP using Change cover in the game menu (···). Games without cover art use their original icon. SteamGridDB is an optional source.

data.name: KeepKey
data.value: Leave blank to keep your existing key

data.name: CoverPrivacy
data.value: Search sends the game's name to SteamGridDB. Windows protects your key for the current user. Covers are stored locally.

data.name: DiagnosticsInfo
data.value: The check only reads display state. The report excludes game paths and keys.

data.name: AboutTitle
data.value: HDR when your game needs it

data.name: AboutBody
data.value: Add the actual game EXE. Launching through the manager or an HDR shortcut enables HDR before the game process starts. Monitoring detects ordinary launches.

data.name: AboutOwnership
data.value: A manual HDR change pauses automatic control. After a crash, the app preserves state that the user may have changed.

data.name: AboutScope
data.value: This manages Windows HDR, not the Auto HDR gaming feature or NVIDIA RTX HDR. Closing the window can hide it in the tray; use Exit to quit.

data.name: AboutPrivacy
data.value: Data stays on your PC. Logs are never uploaded automatically.

data.name: LicensePending
data.value: Free project. An open-source license will be selected before publication.

data.name: UnknownError
data.value: The action could not be completed. Details are available in the local diagnostic log.

data.name: PinInstructions
data.value: Right-click the selected shortcut → Pin to taskbar. If needed, choose Show more options. Windows handles pinning; it has not been confirmed yet.

data.name: IpcFailure
data.value: Could not send the request to the running Auto HDR Manager. Exit the old version from the tray and open the new one.

data.name: GroupingSelectHelp
data.value: Select the game window. The launcher and game may use different EXEs. This check only reads data; it does not modify shortcuts or windows.

data.name: GroupingNoShortcut
data.value: No generated HDR shortcut was found for this game.

data.name: GroupingExplicitFound
data.value: An explicit window ID was read. Matching shortcut and window IDs is the basis for grouping, but does not itself verify the taskbar result. No automatic replacement is performed.

data.name: GroupingNoReadableId
data.value: No explicit window ID was read. This does not prove the absence of a process-level Shell ID. Grouping cannot be guaranteed without a confirmed compatible ID.

data.name: GroupingProcessLimit
data.value: The documented getter for an explicit process Shell ID only reads the calling process. Windows-generated internal IDs cannot be retrieved. GetApplicationUserModelId reports application identity, not necessarily a desktop process Shell ID.

data.name: GroupingWindowGone
data.value: The window exited or its identity was reused. Reopen diagnostics.

data.name: GroupingReadFailed
data.value: The window could not be read again. No identities were changed.

data.name: GroupingCopied
data.value: Copied. The report includes paths and the selected window title; review it before sharing.
